A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualPM research. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references and Appendix A, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original keypoint-transfer and 3D-reconstruction results on PASCAL VOC and Animodel, along with ablations and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and ablations in Table 2.

M1.justification: The canonical-to-posed prediction pipeline, layered amodal representation, confidence-weighted losses and skeleton-fitting procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on synthetic images from one male horse model and evaluate horses, cows and sheep using PASCAL VOC and Animodel. The qualitative scenarios and animation demonstrations are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains A-CSM, MagicPony, Farm3D and 3D-Fauna with identical comparator participation. Table 2 retains the supervised bone-rotation comparator. The newly cited template models are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain PCK@0.1, real-sized and normalized Chamfer distances, the female-horse evaluation subset and exclusion of benchmark poses from training. Training budgets and model settings in Appendix A are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 retains the bone-rotation comparison, four-versus-eight-layer ablation and conditioning ablation. The conditioning examples and failure cases in Figures 8 and 9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both tables retain the same plus/minus reporting for Chamfer distances and point estimates for PCK. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in Tables 1 and 2 is identical after matching citation numbering. For example, horse PCK remains 73.2% and real-sized horse Chamfer distance remains 3.13 ± 2.13 cm. The qualitative results and reported findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The point-map definitions, correspondence and deformation equations, ray-intersection assumptions, layered representation and loss expressions are unchanged. No new formal results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about DualPM, amodal reconstruction, geometric applications and generalization from a single synthetic horse model.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same explanations for pixel-aligned prediction, conditioning-related overfitting and the limited benefit of additional layers. Limitations concerning canonical-space alignment, external occlusion and ambiguous invisible regions are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A is identical apart from citation numbering. Both versions disclose the same architecture, 160×160 outputs, 100k training steps, 33,866 rendered images, 50 actions and 742 environment maps. The project access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a short distinction between templates learned with weak supervision and those learned from 3D data, explicitly mentioning SMPL, SMAL and VAREN. Three references are added, while all 86 earlier references are retained; the broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The added related-work sentence modestly expands the explanation, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose and section order are retained, with text flowing differently around relocated displays.

P2.justification: Existing displays are relocated: Figure 5 moves from page 6 to 7, Table 1 from page 7 to 6, and Table 2 from page 8 to 9. Figure 9 changes columns, and bibliography citation-page backreferences disappear. Figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added passage in Section 2 modestly improves related-work coverage by distinguishing template-learning approaches and explicitly acknowledging SMPL, SMAL and VAREN. This is a limited contextual improvement; the method, empirical evidence, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
